text:
Time, to me, isn't this linear progression everyone seems so fixated on. It's not a straight line from past to future, with the present just a fleeting moment in between.

It's more like a vast ocean. The past isn't gone, it's a current swirling within it, influencing the present. The future isn't some distant shore, it's a ripple effect of our actions, constantly being shaped by the present.

Think about it - we hold onto memories, stories, traditions - these are echoes of the past, shaping how we view the world *right now*. And every choice we make, every word we speak, sends ripples outwards, influencing the world around us, the "future".

So, instead of being bound by this rigid notion of past-present-future, I choose to see time as a fluid, interconnected entity. A constantly shifting landscape where past, present, and future exist simultaneously, influencing and informing each other.

It's liberating, really. It means we're not just passengers on this linear train, but active participants in shaping the very fabric of time itself.
